root_cause.text: Off-by-one error in `iavf_config_rss_reg()` when iterating over RSS key and lookup table arrays due to using `<=` instead of `<`, causing out-of-bounds access one element past the allocated buffer.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly states: "There are off-by-one bugs when configuring RSS hash key and lookup table, causing out-of-bounds reads to memory and out-of-bounds writes to device registers." It explains that the loop bound changed from `i <= I40E_VFQF_{HKEY,HLUT}_MAX_INDEX` (last valid index) to `i <= adapter->rss_{key,lut}_size / 4` (number of dwords), where the last valid index should be `(size/4) - 1`. The patch changes both loops to use `<` instead of `<=`, which is the fix. The KASAN splat confirms an out-of-bounds read exactly one element past the allocated 52-byte region (size 64 kmalloc), matching the off-by-one description.

bic_trace_step.reason: The function loops use 'i <= adapter->rss_key_size / 4' on line 1280 and 'i <= adapter->rss_lut_size / 4' on line 1284. Since the buffers have sizes rss_key_size and rss_lut_size, dividing by 4 gives the number of 4-byte entries. Using '<=' instead of '<' causes the loop to run one extra iteration, accessing dw[adapter->rss_key_size / 4] which is one element past the allocated buffer. This matches the described off-by-one vulnerability. No fix is present; the condition should be '<'.
